data.summary: The 16‑week plan spreads the 3‑hour weekly study load across all AP Physics 1 units, beginning with the student’s weak areas (rotational energy/momentum and oscillations). Each week includes focused topic review, targeted practice problems, and a short quiz. The final two weeks are reserved for mixed review and timed full‑length practice to build stamina before the February exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce rotational kinetic energy and basic SHM concepts.
tasks: Read textbook sections on rotational kinetic energy (6.1) and simple harmonic motion definition (7.1).
Do 5 worked examples for each topic, checking answers against solution guide.
Create a one‑page summary sheet comparing translational and rotational kinetic energy.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of torque‑work relationship and SHM frequency.
tasks: Watch Khan Academy videos on torque and work (6.2) and SHM period/frequency (7.2).
Solve 8 free‑response style problems on torque‑work calculations.
Calculate period and frequency for 5 different pendulum/mass‑spring setups.

weeks.focus: Angular momentum concepts and SHM energy analysis.
tasks: Read and annotate notes on angular momentum and impulse (6.3).
Complete 6 problems converting linear to angular momentum.
Work through 5 energy‑of‑SHM problems, marking each against the scoring rubric.

weeks.focus: Conservation of angular momentum and review of SHM basics.
tasks: Summarize conservation of angular momentum with three real‑world examples.
Do a mixed set of 8 FRQs covering 6.4 and 7.3 (representing/analyzing SHM).
Self‑grade using AP scoring guidelines; note any recurring errors.

weeks.focus: Kinematics in one dimension and vectors.
tasks: Review definitions of scalars/vectors and displacement/velocity/acceleration.
Complete 10 velocity‑time graph problems, then check solutions.
Create flashcards for vector addition rules.
Watch tutorial on projectile motion and relative motion.
Solve 6 projectile problems and 4 relative‑motion scenarios.
Sketch and label vectors for each problem on a separate sheet.
Draw free‑body diagrams for 8 different systems.
Apply Newton’s 2nd law to compute acceleration in each case.
Do a short 5‑minute quiz on identifying forces; review mistakes.

weeks.focus: Newton’s 3rd law and systems of particles.
tasks: Read section on action‑reaction pairs; list 5 real examples.
Solve 6 problems involving center‑of‑mass motion of multiple objects.
Check answers with answer key; annotate any conceptual gaps.
Derive the work‑energy theorem on a blank sheet.
Complete 8 problems mixing work, kinetic energy, and potential energy.
Calculate power for 5 scenarios; record units and reasoning.

weeks.focus: Conservation of energy and power applications.
tasks: Watch a video on energy conservation in roller coasters.
Do 6 FRQs that require stating and applying conservation of energy.
Practice power calculations for machines; verify with solution set.
Summarize momentum definition and impulse‑momentum theorem.
Solve 7 problems on impulse and change in momentum.
Create a quick‑reference table of momentum‑related equations.

weeks.focus: Conservation of linear momentum and collisions.
tasks: Work through 5 elastic and 5 inelastic collision problems.
Check each solution against the AP scoring guide; note where algebra slipped.
Write a one‑paragraph explanation of why momentum is conserved in each case.

weeks.focus: Rotational kinematics and connecting linear‑rotational motion.
tasks: Derive the relationship between linear speed and angular speed.
Complete 6 problems converting between linear and rotational quantities.
Practice rotational kinematics equations with 4 timed questions.

weeks.focus: Torque, rotational inertia, and review of Units 5‑6.
tasks: Calculate torque for 5 different lever setups.
Determine rotational inertia for simple shapes (disc, rod, sphere).
Re‑solve one problem from each of 6.1 and 6.2 to reinforce earlier work.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice (all units).
tasks: Take a 55‑minute full‑length AP Physics 1 practice test (selected sections).
Score the test using the official key; record percent correct per unit.
Review every incorrect answer, writing a brief note on the misconception.

weeks.focus: Final comprehensive review and exam‑day strategy.
tasks: Do a second timed 55‑minute practice test focusing on weak areas identified in week 15.
Create a one‑page cheat‑sheet of key formulas and sign conventions.
Plan exam day logistics (materials, timing, break strategy) and visualize success.

data.final_week_advice: Stay calm, trust your preparation, and use the formula sheet you created as a quick reference. Manage time wisely on the exam: answer all free‑response questions first, then review calculations. Get a good night’s sleep before the test day.
